message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
    --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata=startup-script-url=https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/install_gpu_drivers.sh \
    --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation (`n1-standard-8` ≈ 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM). |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` | When the host machine is replaced, the VM is terminated (default). |
| `--provisioning-model=STANDARD` | Standard provisioning (not preemptible). |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--scopes` | Full Cloud Platform scope – needed for GPU driver installation. |
| `--metadata` | Pass a startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver. |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic if you plan to expose services. |

#### Installing the GPU driver

Create a small shell script (`install_gpu_drivers.sh`) and upload it to a public bucket:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# install_gpu_drivers.sh
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-460   # or newer
sudo reboot
```

Make sure the bucket is publicly readable or grant the instance’s service account permission to read it.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (for programmatic control)

```python
import json
from googleapiclient import discovery
from oauth2client.client import GoogleCredentials

credentials = GoogleCredentials.get_application_default()
service = discovery.build('compute', 'v1', credentials=credentials)

project_id = 'my-gcp-project'
zone = 'us-central1-a'

instance_body = {
    "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
    "machineType": f"projects/{project_id}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
    "disks": [
        {
            "boot": True,
            "autoDelete": True,
            "initializeParams": {
                "diskSizeGb": 100,
                "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
            }
        }
    ],
    "guestAccelerators": [
        {
            "acceleratorCount": 1,
            "acceleratorType": f"projects/{project_id}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
        }
    ],
    "networkInterfaces": [
        {
            "network": "global/networks/default",
            "accessConfigs": [{"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}]
        }
    ],
    "metadata": {
        "items": [
            {
                "key": "startup-script-url",
                "value": "https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/install_gpu_drivers.sh"
            }
        ]
    },
    "scheduling": {
        "preemptible": False,
        "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
        "automaticRestart": True
    },
    "serviceAccounts": [
        {
            "email": "default",
            "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
        }
    ]
}

request = service.instances().insert(project=project_id, zone=zone, body=instance_body)
response = request.execute()
print(json.dumps(response, indent=2))
```

> **Note:**  
> * Replace `<bucket>` with your bucket name.  
> * Ensure the service account has the **Compute Admin** role or at least permissions to create instances and attach GPUs.  
> * The `startup-script-url` is optional but recommended so the NVIDIA driver gets installed automatically.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable the **Compute Engine API** in your project. |
| ✅ | Enable the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** license (`nvidia-driver-460` or newer). |
| ✅ | Grant the instance’s service account the **Cloud Platform** scope or the **Compute Admin** role. |
| ✅ | Make sure the **GPU quota** for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` is available in the chosen zone. |
| ✅ | Verify the **startup script** runs successfully (check serial port logs if it reboots). |

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@<external-ip>
nvidia-smi
```

That’s it! You now have a fully‑functional Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
